limitations: Corpus anchors are verified only when the licensed corpus resolves locally: in corpus-absent mode every anchor is marked verified:false with reason corpus_absent, so this packet is shown with explicitly unverified anchors rather than carried-over pins.

The stored source_revision is a rebind-time snapshot: the engine aggregate hash includes untracked non-ignored files, so it is not reproducible after the rebind report was written; the stale gate is the per-input live sha256.

Two of the eight dispute cards are conflicted (competence, temporal_qualification) and six are unresolved; no card carries a resolved verdict, and a conflicted or unresolved card is a boundary, not a resolution.
The definition family has no owning section 3 row (no_owning_row) and the competence family ceiling is only proposed, so the eight-family set is not uniformly bounded.
No human-labelled gold set exists here and none is implied.
No runtime surface exists or is promised: no normative IR, no rule graph and no applicability evaluator.
The recommendation is advisory only: it is not the owner's consent, and the agent does not select an option for the owner.

ir_question.prompt: Which bounded normative IR alternative should the owner adopt: A family_typed_record_ir, B single_facet_slot_rule_record, or C abstention_first_candidates_only? The owner may also reject all three or defer the decision. No option is preselected and no answer is assumed here.

options.label: adopt family_typed_record_ir
options.consequences: S03 would mint and validate eight record kinds plus a shared envelope and a separate link record, and would have to define Condition, Exception and Defeater in section 3 before any family payload can carry a guard or a defeat.
what_it_cannot_prove: It cannot prove the legal correctness of a family classification, a record payload or a reading: separation is a structural property, not a legal conclusion.
It cannot prove that the eight record kinds exhaust every normative distinction a source provision carries.
It cannot prove that two records anchored to the same provision describe one norm; composition stays a later decision.

options.label: adopt single_facet_slot_rule_record
options.consequences: S03 would extend the existing ln-applicability NormRule spine (RC11-F04a) with a deontic operator, a definition scope and a competence source, and would have to define all six normative section 3 rows; facet-default policy and composition would be the first runtime surface to fail-closed.
what_it_cannot_prove: It cannot prove the legal correctness of a facet value or of a composed rule: one record with facets is a representation, not an adjudication.
It cannot prove that a missing facet is a deliberate absence rather than an unrecorded family; facet defaults are exactly where a silent collapse can hide.
It cannot prove that facet values on one record describe a single norm rather than several norms that share an anchor.

options.label: adopt abstention_first_candidates_only
options.consequences: S03 would build only candidate emission and the fail-closed Unknown or Conflict verdicts; composition, facet defaults and applicability stay deferred and the section 3 rows stay deferred-undefined.
what_it_cannot_prove: It cannot prove the legal correctness of a family classification or the absence of a norm: it produces candidates and Unknown outcomes, not conclusions.
It cannot prove rule composition, precedence, exception defeat or case applicability, because no rule is composed.
It cannot prove that the emitted candidate set is complete for a provision.

options.label: reject all three alternatives
options.consequences: No bounded normative IR is adopted now: the three alternatives stay presented and unadopted, S03 has no adopted scope to build against, and a later decision must reopen the same question with a fresh rebind.
what_it_cannot_prove: It cannot prove that the alternatives are wrong, only that none is accepted now.
It cannot prove that abstention is safe: rejecting all three leaves the bounded IR undecided.
It cannot prove anything about the legal correctness of any reading.

options.label: defer the decision
options.consequences: The decision moves to a later slice: the packet stays proposed and unadopted, S03 cannot start from an adopted scope, and the question must be re-presented with a fresh rebind.
what_it_cannot_prove: It cannot prove that a later decision will be easier or better informed.
It cannot prove that the deferred question stays bounded.
It cannot prove anything about the legal correctness of any reading.

recommendation.rationale: All three alternatives are source-bound and none is adopted. C is recommended because it defines no new section 3 term and composes no rule, so it stays inside the deferred-undefined boundary that RC28-F18 declares, while A and B both require deferred section 3 rows before any payload can be built. This is a recommendation only: it is not consent, and the owner may accept any option, reject all three or defer.

f13_question.prompt: Should the owner adopt a source-level amendment operation-candidate contract as the bridge to the temporal compiler, or keep amendment operations deferred? This is a separate decision from the bounded normative IR question.

options.label: adopt a source-level amendment operation-candidate contract (design-only, owning contracts first)
options.consequences: F13 gets an owning contract for replace, new wording, insert, remove and repeal candidates with nested target scope and quoted operands; an extracted operation stays a candidate and is never an admitted MicroOperation, LegislativeEffect or InForce, and no automatic operation reinterpretation happens on missing operands.
what_it_cannot_prove: It cannot prove that an extracted operation is legally correct or admitted.
It cannot prove amendment coverage over the corpus.

options.label: keep amendment operations deferred
options.consequences: Amendment syntax stays an unowned gap: the bridge to the temporal compiler stays missing, and the owning slice must reopen F13 with a fresh rebind before any bounded temporal replay can rely on it.
what_it_cannot_prove: It cannot prove that deferral is safe, only that the decision is not taken here.
It cannot prove anything about the correctness of any amendment reading.

recommendation.rationale: RC28-F13 is high severity and design class, but its owning surface is not this decision: the review asks for owning contracts first, the recorded ownership sits with the amendment and temporal-compiler work, and this packet's scope is the bounded normative IR. Keeping amendment operations deferred answers F13 with an explicit boundary instead of a silent omission. This is a recommendation only and is not consent; no answer leaves F13 at HOLD.
